statement: Biopsy-sized samples from autopsied cardiac allografts were compared with larger sections of the same hearts; the authors concluded that routine biopsies may underestimate middle grades of rejection.
supports: A direct cardiac precedent for using autopsy tissue to study spatial sampling limitations of small biopsies.
does_not_establish: Not longitudinal comparison of living-patient biopsy with subsequent autopsy, not an AI training study, and historical grades must not be equated with modern 0R-3R. Abstract-only review.
method_or_result: Biopsy-sized samples obtained directly from 22 autopsied human cardiac allografts and compared with large tissue sections; historical rejection grading.

statement: The study re-examined available post-transplant endomyocardial biopsies and transplanted-heart autopsy tissue, with two cardiac pathologists blinded to prior reports, to relate pathology including acute myocardial injury to clinical outcomes.
supports: A clinical-pathological precedent for connecting biopsy and autopsy records in a heart-transplant cohort.
does_not_establish: Not a combined biopsy/autopsy AI training study or proof that autopsy supervision improves rejection prediction. Does not imply every one of the 47 patients had paired autopsy tissue or that acute myocardial injury equals rejection.
method_or_result: Single-center retrospective study of 47 heart-transplant recipients who died or underwent retransplantation; review of available endomyocardial biopsies and transplanted hearts at autopsy.

statement: Two tuberculosis autopsy cases supplied annotated positive acid-fast bacilli, and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases supplied background/artifact examples for CNN training, followed by application to bronchoscopy specimens.
supports: A concrete noncardiac precedent for transferring lesion-level information from autopsy tissue to biopsy analysis.
does_not_establish: Bacillus detection is not cardiac rejection grading. The source ties positive training material to autopsy and negative material to biopsy; it does not eliminate specimen-source confounding or establish the benefit of adding autopsy data over a matched biopsy-only baseline. Methods 2.1 mentions 14 validation cases whereas the abstract reports 42; no validation sample-size or efficacy claim is indexed.
method_or_result: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast-bacillus detection using CNN training with two pulmonary tuberculosis autopsy cases and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases.

statement: A model pretrained on GTEx tissue-type recognition was transferred to renal glomerulus, arteriole and artery segmentation; the paper identifies GTEx WSIs as autopsy tissue.
supports: A noncardiac example of autopsy-derived representation pretraining transferred to biopsy histology analysis.
does_not_establish: Does not establish benefit for heart-transplant rejection, equivalence between biopsy and autopsy, or an advantage over an already pretrained UNI encoder. GTEx pretraining used multiple organs, not a rejection cohort.
method_or_result: Renal histological structure segmentation with transfer learning, comparing random initialization, a glomerulus model, GTEx tissue-type pretraining and ImageNet pretraining.

statement: Heart-transplant autopsies included both graft-related and non-graft-related deaths; infection was the most frequent cause of death. The abstract also reports moderate/severe ACR in a patient with a recently negative biopsy.
supports: Autopsy availability or death alone cannot define a rejection-positive label; specimen-level diagnosis and biopsy-to-death chronology require review.
does_not_establish: A recent negative biopsy followed by rejection at autopsy does not distinguish biopsy sampling error from interval progression or treatment effects. Does not justify retrospectively changing the earlier biopsy label or demonstrate an AI training benefit. Abstract-only review.
method_or_result: Retrospective 1990-2023 heart-transplant autopsy review: 88 identified cases, with 15 excluded from cause-of-death evaluation because slides were unavailable.

statement: In the renal vessel-segmentation comparison, GTEx pretraining outperformed random initialization but ImageNet pretraining achieved higher MCC than GTEx for glomeruli, arterioles and arteries.
supports: Autopsy-derived pretraining is a comparator to test, not an assumed improvement.
does_not_establish: Does not rank pretraining strategies for cardiac rejection or show that more autopsy tissue will resolve rare-positive patient scarcity.
method_or_result: Renal vessel segmentation; Figure 3 compares initialization strategies on holdout WSIs.
